title: A C interface for a C++ class
hints: Define `struct BagHandle { StoneBag bag; };` in the implementation. Callers only see the incomplete declaration `struct BagHandle;`, so they can hold pointers but never look inside.
One small guard function (like lesson 2.06's barrier) that every exported function calls keeps the error handling identical everywhere.
requirements: Every exported function has a plain C signature and is `extern "C"`.
No exception can leave any of the functions.
Bags are created and destroyed only by the library, and live bags are counted.
The heaviest name is returned through a caller buffer with the length always reported.
stretch: Add `bag_last_error(char* buffer, int capacity)` that returns the message of the last failure on the calling thread (lesson 3.02 does this properly).
